Get ready for all of the investors in frontier model companies to suddenly flip to regulatory capture mode today 

Their investments in frontier model companies are currently at risk/capped because the biggest buyers of tokens are embracing open-source models: vertical AI companies, the government and enterprises 

That’s all this is about: stopping open source — which I’ve been saying on the pod for two years 

If you want safety, you want disclosure — and open source is the ultimate disclosure process

Currently… all of the frontier companies, and others, are experimenting with different types of cloud computers that power GrokBot, GPT Work, Meta Muse, Claude Cowork, and countless others.

It’s hard to tell what works best, so I’m limiting my use of the above-mentioned tools to experimentation. I’m not committing to any one of them because I don’t know what the right cloud agent setup is yet… nobody does. Especially for business.

What I do know is that macOS is elite.

Codex + Astra can do basically anything on a Mac. I can remotely control Codex from my phone, iPad, or another lightweight laptop. My Mac has 48GB of RAM, it’s fast, it has my browser with all the accounts I need already signed in, and I can fully control the computer remotely from any device.

Codex is getting scary good at controlling advanced software through computer use, like DaVinci Resolve and Premiere. It has access to all of my videos on an external hard drive, and it’s plugged into all of the tools I use for work, like Notion and Google Drive.

This setup is more powerful than OpenClaw, and more predictable. 

It is however, token guzzling.

I get the argument that the value of mathematics is often in the ideas developed while attacking a problem, not just the final answer.

What I don’t understand is why those ideas can only be developed while a problem remains "unsolved."

If AI solves a problem, humans can still find better proofs, different proofs, generalizations, explanations, new techniques, etc.

What actually disappears is the prize for being first. Which...seems like a very different concern.
